title: Hairpin lace cushion cover
excerpt: A textured cushion cover in DK yarn worked with hairpin lace strips. The strips are joined across the cushion front and backed with a plain crochet panel that folds over to close.
sourceNotes: A cushion front in hairpin lace with a plain dc envelope back. The strips run horizontally across the front, joined with a double crochet joining row.

glossaryTerms.definition: A two-part cushion back where two overlapping plain crochet rectangles fold over the cushion pad to create a self-closing opening.
A row of double crochets worked through loops from two adjacent hairpin strips at once to join them into a single fabric panel.

crochet.gaugeText: Each hairpin strip = 5 cm wide with prongs set 5 cm apart.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Fits a 45 cm square cushion pad.

Work each strip to 100 loops per side (about 45 cm long). Remove carefully from the frame. Join the strips side by side: hold two strips together, insert hook through 1 loop from each, and work a double crochet through both. Continue alternating loops down the length. Repeat for each pair until all 9 strips form a square panel.
Chain 68. Work dc in rows until each back panel measures 30 cm. Fasten off.

Place the front with right side up. Overlap the two back panels at the centre by 10 cm, right side down. Sew around all four edges with the tapestry needle. Turn right side out and insert the cushion pad.
